method: Shipped demo/main.tscn rendered with the normal player input adapter disabled only for scripted QA. Public set_move_intent API drove the paths. Reviewed 24 actual viewport PNGs as two montages, plus full-size stair ascent/descent frames.

checks.evidence: Body climbs from ground to .752m, stops on landing, turns and descends to ground. Full-body views show sensible bent-knee stepping and no visible body suspension, persistent foot drag, knee reversal or deep tread penetration.

checks.scenario: left stair side diagonal rubbing and exit
checks.evidence: Both terrain-side and outside camera views inspected. Body stays at ground height (~.0019m), feet keep stepping, turning away releases the path without an idle freeze or a raised/floating body.
SpringArm shortens before the wall and does not expose the view from inside the wall. Character remains in front of the camera.

limitations: When the character is pushed close to a wall behind the camera, the camera becomes an extreme upper-body close-up. This is a cosmetic limitation of the current SpringArm obstruction response, not wall penetration.

This terrain review used sampled rendered frames rather than a claim that every display frame was manually inspected. Input/orbit combinations, zoom bounds, focus release and no-autoplay are covered separately by tests/controls.gd.
